summary:
DalaSync is an AI-powered land intelligence platform that helps farmers make smarter, data-driven agricultural decisions.

The platform transforms complex satellite observations, soil information, climate data, and geospatial analysis into actionable insights. Farmers can select or draw their land on an interactive map and automatically generate a comprehensive Land Passport containing information about soil characteristics, environmental conditions, climate patterns, and land potential.

Using NASA Earth observation data alongside complementary geospatial and soil datasets, DalaSync analyzes agricultural conditions and helps farmers evaluate land before purchasing or leasing it. The platform also aims to support crop suitability assessment, yield scenario analysis, and sustainable crop rotation planning through its AI-powered Agronomist.

Our solution addresses the growing challenges of soil degradation, water scarcity, drought, and climate variability, particularly relevant to agriculture in Kazakhstan and other arid regions.

By making satellite-based intelligence accessible and understandable, DalaSync empowers farmers to reduce uncertainty, optimize agricultural investments, and build more sustainable and climate-resilient farming practices.
details:
Project Details

DalaSync is designed as an intelligent agricultural decision-support platform that connects satellite Earth observations, soil data, geospatial technology, and AI to help farmers understand their land and make better farming decisions.

How It Works

Farmers begin by selecting their agricultural land on an interactive map or defining their field boundaries. The platform uses geospatial analysis and external environmental datasets to build a digital Land Passport for each field.

The Land Passport organizes important information about the selected territory, including soil characteristics, geographic location, and environmental conditions. Satellite imagery from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS) provides a visual perspective of the land and its surroundings, while soil information is enriched through SoilGrids data.

An integrated AI-powered Agronomist interprets the available information and generates understandable, rule-based agricultural insights. Instead of presenting raw scientific data, DalaSync aims to translate it into practical recommendations that farmers can use when evaluating land and planning agricultural activities.

Benefits and Intended Impact

DalaSync aims to:

  • Help farmers evaluate agricultural land before purchasing or leasing it.
  • Make satellite and soil information accessible without requiring specialized scientific knowledge.
  • Identify potential environmental and agricultural risks.
  • Support informed crop selection and sustainable crop rotation decisions.
  • Reduce uncertainty in agricultural investments and resource planning.
  • Encourage more responsible soil and water management.

Our initial focus is Kazakhstan, where agriculture faces significant challenges related to drought, water scarcity, soil degradation, and climate variability. The platform is designed to be adaptable to other agricultural regions with similar environmental challenges.

Technology and Development Tools

Our team developed the platform using modern web technologies and geospatial tools:

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript.
  • Styling and UI: Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Lucide.
  • Interactive mapping: Leaflet.
  • Satellite imagery: NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services).
  • Soil information: SoilGrids.
  • Geospatial services: Geocoding and geographic field selection.
  • Backend: Next.js API architecture and data-processing modules.
  • AI and analytics: Rule-based agricultural analysis and an AI Agronomist concept.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of DalaSync is the combination of several traditionally disconnected technologies into one accessible agricultural intelligence platform.

Instead of making farmers search through satellite databases, scientific reports, and environmental datasets independently, DalaSync brings this information together in a single interface and transforms it into a field-specific Land Passport.

Our approach focuses on explainable intelligence: agricultural insights should be understandable, traceable to available data, and useful for real-world decisions rather than simply generating generic AI responses.

Factors Considered

During development, we considered data accessibility, scientific reliability, regional agricultural conditions, usability for farmers without technical expertise, scalability, and the limitations of satellite observations.

We also considered the importance of distinguishing measured environmental data from estimates and recommendations. Our goal is not to replace farmers or agronomists, but to give them better information and tools to make more informed decisions.

Our vision is to make satellite-powered agricultural intelligence accessible to every farmer, starting with Kazakhstan.
